correctness.rationale: The proof was reconstructed from the S-SEG update: in complex coordinates each sample is multiplication by s+i, so one same-sample extragradient step has multiplier m_s(gamma)=1-s gamma+i(2s gamma^2-gamma). Exact algebra yields |m_+|^2|m_-|^2=16 gamma^8-4 gamma^4+1 and E|m_s|^2=1+2 gamma^2+4 gamma^4. The strong law gives the almost-sure exponent. At gamma=1/sqrt(2), the radial multipliers are sqrt(2)-1 and sqrt(2)+1, making the log-radius a simple symmetric random walk. The included standard-library checker independently replays the algebraic identities; finite computation is not used to justify the probability theorems.

value.rationale: The claim gives a sharp closed-form pathwise stability boundary for a sampling-sensitive S-SEG model directly motivated by the 2026 source. More importantly, below the boundary the last iterate converges exponentially almost surely while its second moment diverges exponentially. This is a substantive, exact warning that L2 growth can be qualitatively opposite to pathwise stability under multiplicative stochastic extragradient dynamics, and the critical random-walk law identifies the boundary mechanism rather than merely giving a numerical threshold.
